description:
Why this issue exists: state/version.rs bump_state() executes INSERT ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE to increment the state counter, then a separate SELECT to read the new value. Under concurrent writers these are two independent transactions: another writer can increment again between the INSERT and the SELECT, causing bump_state() to return a state value it did not create. JMAP RFC 8620 §6.3 requires that every method call that changes state returns the exact new state it produced.

What needs to be done: Use a single statement with RETURNING (SQLite ≥3.35) to atomically increment and return the new value: UPDATE state_versions SET version = version + 1 WHERE ... RETURNING version. This eliminates the race window and guarantees the returned state string matches what was written.
title: bump_state: two-query pattern has TOCTOU race under concurrent writes
